purpose: Model Minecraft world-play machinery as a causal semantic graph rather than isolated blocks or scripts.

core_model.invariant: Every player-meaningful mechanism should be traceable from perceivable input through state/logic to effect and feedback; hidden implementation may support the experience but should not create unexplained or contradictory canonical state.

capabilities: impulse, chain, and repeating execution modes
invoke functions and commands that read/write scoreboards, storage, entities, blocks, inventories, effects, text, sounds, particles, structures and world state
ux_strengths: can be physically embedded in authored machinery
excellent bridge from redstone events to high-level scripted effects

capabilities: torches and circuit topology for boolean logic
ux_strengths: supports puzzles whose causal structure can be learned by players

capabilities: opening a trapped chest emits redstone power
container inventory can be read through comparator behavior
container contents can encode puzzle/state inputs
pairs naturally with hoppers, droppers, dispensers and command logic
ux_strengths: can make loot/opening itself a cause rather than merely a reward
risks: surprise traps without signaling can feel arbitrary
inventory mutation must remain synchronized with semantic state

examples: sculk sensors and calibrated sculk sensors
comparators reading containers and selected block states
ux_strengths: allow location, motion, sound/vibration, projectile, time and object-state to become gameplay inputs
produce visible consequences that help players infer causal relationships

capabilities: command macros where supported by the data-pack function system
26.3 compute command and compute-backed data mutation
persistent counters, flags and numeric state
structured command storage for non-entity state
bridge between embodied redstone and hidden semantic rules
data_driven_primitives.design_rule: Prefer these for authored semantic state over treating redstone wire power as canonical narrative truth.

capabilities: 26.3 richer block matching and slot-source conditions
custom recipes and 26.3 data-driven potion recipes
26.3 block_transformer component: an item can transform a block with configured sound/particles
custom item interaction semantics through components
26.3 template processors and volume-match block predicates
invisible configurable hit/interaction surfaces that record attacks and right-click interactions
use_cases: precise UX surfaces decoupled from visible block geometry

capabilities: block, item and text displays with arbitrary transforms and interpolation

interaction_and_presentation_primitives.ux_rule: Feedback should make the causal result legible without over-explaining the puzzle.

capabilities: textures, models, sounds, fonts and UI assets
custom item/block presentation through model/data-component systems
server command can request add/list/remove/clear post effects on players
effects are client resource-pack post-processing shaders
interaction_and_presentation_primitives.caveat: Server cannot know whether a client-side post effect actually rendered; treat as requested presentation state, not authoritative world truth.

semantic_composition_patterns.example: Player places weighted item -> comparator threshold satisfied -> piston route opens -> lamp/note confirms success.
Player opens trapped chest -> event checks narrative flags -> records theft -> changes faction state -> locks route/spawns response -> audio/text/world change explains consequence.
Unique mechanism destroyed -> durable fact prevents regeneration -> later repair requires explicit resource/state transition.
A custom tool transforms only approved ritual blocks, emits particles/sound, and advances a puzzle state.

extraction_targets: datapack function call graph and scheduled/tick entry points
evaluation_questions: Can a player perceive the cause before or soon after the effect?
Is the mechanism state reconstructible and deterministic?
Does physical state agree with semantic/canonical state?
Are failure, retry and success states clearly distinguishable?
Can the mechanism survive chunk unload/reload and server restart?
Can simultaneous players produce races or double-consume unique state?
Does regeneration overwrite a committed consequence?
Is hidden command/datapack machinery doing work that should be visible or explained diegetically?
Can a generator safely edit the area without severing causal edges?
Can static analysis recover enough of the graph to drive automated tours/persona tests?
